title: Finite affine descent of internal-Hom bounds and uniform integral direct-image bounds
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$, with the scheme, coefficient-sheaf and operation conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $W$ be any finite-type $k$-scheme, not necessarily separated over $k$, and let $d_W\geq0$ satisfy $\dim W\leq d_W$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. On the small pro-etale site use the intrinsic finite-torsion constructibility and finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and ambient derived internal Hom $H_W$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

For integers $a\leq b$ and $c\leq e$, and $P,Q\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A_n)$ of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,e]$, respectively, $H_W(P,Q)$ is bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude in $[c-b-2d_W,e-a+2d_W]$. The bound is valid on $W$ itself for a finite affine cover with this single dimension bound; it requires no separatedness of $W$ and no site-perfectness of either input.

Use the actual completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$. For $P,Q\in D^b_c(W,R)$ in the derived-complete integral sense [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], write $P_n,Q_n$ for their reductions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. If every $P_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and every $Q_n$ in $[c,e]$, then $H_W(P,Q)=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_W}(P,Q)$ is derived complete and belongs to $D^b_c(W,R)=D^b_{ctf}(W,R)$. Its evaluation-defined comparison
$$H_W(P,Q)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_W}(A_n)_W\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_W}(P_n,Q_n)$$
is an isomorphism in the derived category at every $n$, and all reductions have Tor amplitude in $[c-b-2d_W,e-a+2d_W]$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes and let $d_X\geq0$ bound $\dim X$. If $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and all $K_n$ have Tor interval $[u,v]$, then $Rf_*K$ is derived complete, belongs to $D^b_c(Y,R)=D^b_{ctf}(Y,R)$, and the canonical maps
$$(Rf_*K)_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(K_n)$$
are isomorphisms in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ compatible with quotient transitions. Every reduction has Tor interval $[u,v+2d_X]$, hence also that common cohomological bound. All assertions include empty schemes, for which one may take dimension bound zero.

proof.text: Fix a finite level. By lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin choose bounded constructible etale origins $P',Q'$ for the intrinsic pro-etale objects $P,Q$. Clause (ii) of lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude gives precisely the intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,e]$ for these origins. Apply thm-sf-hom-ctf to $W,P',Q'$ and the supplied $d_W$: it gives bounded constructibility and Tor interval $I=[c-b-2d_W,e-a+2d_W]$ for $H_{\mathrm{et}}(P',Q')$. Its statement permits every finite-type scheme; separatedness and site-perfectness are absent from its general assertion. In particular the theorem already supplies the finite-affine-cover descent with a single dimension bound; applying it on $W$ does not require affine intersections or separatedness of $W$.

The first origin $P'$ is now in $D^b_{ctf}$ and the second is bounded constructible, so thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible identifies $H_W(P,Q)$ with $\nu_W^*H_{\mathrm{et}}(P',Q')$ in the derived category. Clause (i) of lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude transfers bounded constructibility and the same interval $I$ to this object. This proves the entire finite-level assertion for arbitrary intrinsic inputs; the comparison theorem assumes no site-perfectness. The exact intrinsic coefficient realization identifies the fixed-scalar ambient Hom with the recorded Hom-complex localization by lem-sf-intrinsic-site-hom-transport. Compose this with the two input origin isomorphisms, and transport constructibility and the exact Tor interval by isomorphism invariance.

For integral $P,Q$, use lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction on the actual ring sheaf $B=\widehat R_W$. Since $Q$ is complete, $H_B(P,Q)$ is complete, and its stated evaluation-transpose comparison $F_nH_B(P,Q)\to H_{B_n}(P_n,Q_n)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. Apply Steps 1–2 to each $P_n,Q_n$: the hypothesis supplies the same two Tor intervals for every $n$, hence their Homs are constructible with the same interval $I$. Taking the degree-zero coefficient ring sheaf as test module in the definition of Tor amplitude also bounds their cohomology by $I$. Completeness, constructibility of every reduction, and this uniform cohomological bound are exactly def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed. Thus the ambient Hom belongs to $D^b_c(W,R)$; its uniform Tor bound places it in $D^b_{ctf}(W,R)$ by def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude. The equality of the two integral categories is the scheme-general assertion of lem-coef-integral-residue-tor, so no separatedness is introduced here. The legacy completeness supplied by integralHomReduction is converted to IsSfDerivedComplete by lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison. Isomorphism invariance of intrinsic constructibility is supplied by lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated. The tensor-unit support argument chooses a K-flat resolution, so it is valid for the unbounded ambient derived category.

For $f$ and $K$ in the last paragraph, cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale applied to each $K_n$ gives bounded constructibility and Tor interval $J=[u,v+2d_X]$ for $Rf_{*,n}K_n$. It requires separatedness of $f$, which is assumed, but not separatedness of either scheme over $k$. The same $d_X,u,v$ work at every level. By def-weil-derived-direct-image the integral $Rf_*K$ is the derived limit of these finite direct images with the prescribed quotient transitions. Lem-sf-complete-direct-image-reduction states that this object is complete and that the canonical scalar adjunct of each limit projection is an isomorphism. These are exactly the reduction maps asserted here.

source.place: lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (Tag 099N), parts (1),(3),(4), and lemma-naive-completion; with the perfect-coefficient projection formula of Tag 0944

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-direct-image-reduction-transitions to obtain the precise adjacent transition square for the prescribed projection adjuncts. The comparisons in Step 4 respect quotient transitions: writing $\pi_n$ for the limit projections and $t_{m,n}$ for a tower transition ($m\ge n$), their defining cone relation is $t_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$. Taking the scalar-extension adjuncts, with the canonical successive-reduction identifications, gives exactly the transition square for the reduction comparisons; this uses their specified projection normalization, not a choice of isomorphisms. By Step 4 all reductions are constructible with Tor interval $J$; testing on the coefficient ring sheaf gives the same cohomological interval. Completeness and the defining uniform-bound criterion therefore put $Rf_*K$ in $D^b_c(Y,R)$, and the uniform Tor criterion puts it in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,R)$. The category equality is again lem-coef-integral-residue-tor. On an empty scheme the empty covering is a covering, so every sheaf is zero by the sheaf axiom; all the complexes above are zero and the bounds with dimension zero remain valid.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-caed00577 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, all 11 cited statements, the relevant proofs of thm-sf-hom-ctf and cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale, and the parent fix-lem-tensor-adjunction (blueprint Step 2 and split step 1). There are no new nodes, the statement is unchanged and nothing is weakened. Step 1 (origin lemma, then comparison-tor-amplitude (ii), then thm-sf-hom-ctf) is correct: thm-sf-hom-ctf is stated for any finite-type k-scheme and proved by a finite affine cover with one m, so it covers nonseparated W. Its interval [c-b-2m,d-a+2m] matches the item's. Step 2 (thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible needs only ctf first and D^b_c second input; clause (i) transfers the interval I) is correct. Step 3: lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction works over the same B=lim (A_n)_X, and its c_n is the item's evaluation-transpose map. Completeness comes from Q being complete. Testing with N=B_n gives the uniform support required by def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, and residue-tor gives D^b_c=D^b_ctf. Step 4: cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale applies levelwise (f separated finite type, dim X<=d), and lem-sf-complete-direct-image-reduction gives completeness and the prescribed projection-adjoint isomorphisms. Step 5 (transition square by adjunction naturality) is genuinely elementary. Small cases checked: a point gives the sharp [c-b,e-a]; i_*A against A on a curve sits in degree 2, inside [-2,2], so the 2d enlargement is needed; A_1 over A_2 is not ctf; the empty scheme is fine. The route departures to sk-thm-sf-hom-ctf and sk-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf are accepted as generic tool uses declared in split_report. There is no cycle and no SGA. Batch-5 flag: lem-pod-derived-exact-square-composition, reached via lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison, is generic exact-functor derived-square coherence and not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so the flag is accepted.
